passages.title: Mount Everest
passages.text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. Its elevation of 8,848.86 m (29,031.7 ft) was most recently established in 2020 by Chinese and Nepali authorities. The China-Nepal border runs across its summit point. Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first official ascent on 29 May 1953. The mountain was named after Sir George Everest, the Surveyor General of India from 1830 to 1843. In Nepali it is called Sagarmatha ("forehead of the sky"). Climbers usually take 6 to 9 weeks, e.g. to acclimatise at Base Camp (5,364 m).

passages.title: Ocean acidification
passages.text: Ocean acidification is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth's ocean. Between 1950 and 2020, the average pH of the ocean surface fell from approximately 8.15 to 8.05. Carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from human activities, e.g. burning coal, oil and gas, are the main cause. Seawater is slightly basic (pH > 7), so the process is a shift toward neutral rather than a change to acidic water. Today the surface ocean has a mean pH of about 8.1. Shell-building organisms such as oysters, clams and corals are harmed because carbonate ions become scarcer.

passages.title: Washing machine drain pump
passages.text: Replacing a washing machine drain pump takes about 45 minutes. Step 1: Unplug the machine and turn off both water taps. Step 2: Remove the lower front panel (two 8 mm screws on most models). Step 3: Put towels on the floor; about 0.5 L of water will run out. Step 4: Disconnect the hoses and the wiring plug, then unscrew the pump. Step 5: Fit the new pump and test for leaks on a short rinse cycle. Never run the machine with the panel off.

passages.title: Nairobi
passages.text: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya. Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) lies about 15 km south-east of the city centre. A taxi to the centre costs approx. KSh 2,500 and takes 30 to 60 minutes, depending on traffic. Matatus (privately run minibuses) are cheap, e.g. KSh 100 for a short ride, but often crowded. Nairobi National Park is only 7 km from the centre; its gates open at 6 a.m. and close at 7 p.m. daily. M-Pesa, a mobile money service, is accepted almost everywhere.

passages.title: St Paul's Cathedral
passages.text: St. Paul's Cathedral stands on Ludgate Hill, the highest point of the City of London. It was designed by Sir Christopher Wren and completed in 1710. Dr. Samuel Johnson is buried in Westminster Abbey, not in St. Paul's. The cross on top of the dome is 111 metres above the ground. Adult visitors, including those from the U.S. and Canada, pay 25 pounds for entry. Services are free to attend.

passages.title: J. R. R. Tolkien
passages.text: J. R. R. Tolkien was an English writer and philologist. He wrote The Hobbit (1937) and The Lord of the Rings (1954-55). His friend C. S. Lewis, author of the Narnia books, taught at Oxford with him. Tolkien was born in Bloemfontein, in what is now South Africa, on 3 January 1892. He died in Bournemouth on 2 September 1973.

passages.title: Mind the gap
passages.text: "Mind the gap" is a warning first used on the London Underground in 1968. The best-known recording was made by the actor Oswald Laurence... Its voice became familiar to millions of travellers. Embankment station still plays his original recording. "It is a little piece of history," a spokesman said. The Underground opened in 1863 as the world's first underground railway.

passages.title: pH
passages.text: Pure water has a pH of 7.0 at 25 °C. Lemon juice has a pH of about 2.0, and household bleach about 12.5. The scale usually runs from 0 to 14. A change of one unit means a tenfold change in hydrogen ion concentration (e.g. pH 5 is ten times more acidic than pH 6). At 50 °C pure water has a pH of about 6.63, yet it is still neutral.

passages.title: Eiffel Tower
passages.text: The Eiffel Tower stands on the Champ de Mars in Paris. Its height is 330 m. It was the tallest man-made structure in the world until 1930. Gustave Eiffel's company built it for the World's Fair of 1889.

passages.title: Bleeding a radiator
passages.text: To bleed a radiator, follow these steps. 1. Turn the heating off and let the radiator cool. 2. Hold a cloth under the bleed valve. 3. Turn the radiator key a quarter turn anticlockwise until water appears. 4. Close the valve and check that the boiler pressure is about 1.5 bar.

4. Close the valve and check that the boiler pressure is about 1.5 bar.

passages.title: Fort Worth
passages.text: Fort Worth, often written Ft. Worth, is a city in Texas. It was named in 1849 after Gen. William J. Worth. The city lies about 50 km west of Dallas. Its stockyards were once among the largest in the U.S. Today they are a historic district.

passages.title: Carbon monoxide
passages.text: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a colourless, odourless and poisonous gas. It is produced when fuels such as gas, oil, coal and wood do not burn fully. Breathing it in can cause headaches, dizziness, nausea and loss of consciousness. Carbon dioxide (CO2), by contrast, is produced by complete burning and by breathing. Fit a CO alarm in every room that has a fuel-burning appliance. If the alarm sounds, open doors and windows, turn off appliances and get into fresh air at once.

passages.title: Treating stream water
passages.text: Water from a stream is not safe to drink untreated. Boil it at a rolling boil for at least 1 minute (3 minutes above 2,000 m). Unscented household bleach can be used instead: add 2 drops per litre of clear water and wait 30 minutes. Cloudy water should first be filtered through a clean cloth.

passages.text: Never replace a fuse with one of a higher rating, e.g. a 13 A fuse in place of a 5 A fuse. Keep spare fuses, a torch, insulated pliers, etc. Turn off the main switch before opening the fuse box. A 3 A fuse suits appliances up to about 700 W.

passages.title: Grace Hopper
passages.text: Grace Hopper earned a Ph.D. in mathematics from Yale in 1934. She joined the U.S. Navy Reserve in 1943. Later, as Rear Adm. Hopper, she promoted COBOL. The ship USS Hopper (DDG-70) is named after her.
